sources.citation: Henson, Bonnie J. & Angela Kluge. 2011. A sociolinguistic survey of the Gbe language communities of Benin and Togo, Volume 5: Xwla language area. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2011-017. Dallas: SIL International. 43 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sociolinguistic survey (word lists, RA-RTT comprehension, vitality). Sec. 3 'Previous linguistic research' (pp. 5-7) names only Capo 1986/1991 (comparative Gbe phonology; Xwla = Capo's 'Phla') and SIL/CNL word lists as prior work. 'accent' only in the folk sense: sec. 6.1 p. 11 'no dialects of Xwla, though there are distinguishable accents from one village to another'; sec. 6.1.3 contact 'begins to impact the Xwla tones, accents and even words'. Covers western (Togo/Grand-Popo) and eastern (Ouémé) Xwla.

sources.citation: Kluge, Angela. 2011. A sociolinguistic survey of the Gbe language communities of Benin and Togo: Gbe language family overview. SIL ESR 2011-012. 21 pp; and Kluge, Angela. 2008. The Gbe language varieties of West Africa: a quantitative analysis of lexical and grammatical features. SIL ESR 2008-023. 214 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Classification/lexicostatistics; Xwla split into western (Adamé) and eastern (Djeffa, 'Movolo' per Capo 1999) varieties; word lists entered without tone. Cites Henson & Kluge 1999 unpublished Xwla survey (= 2011 ESR 2011-017).

Gbe lects treated as tone languages; no word-stress statement.
